What is Impermanent Loss?

Published by TradeHQ. Site creator and editorial approach: Anuga Weerasinghe. This page has no recorded editorial review date.

DETAILED DEFINITION

For a fee-free, full-range constant-product pool initially balanced by value, compare the liquidity-provider position with holding the originally deposited assets. If their relative price changes by a factor r and arbitrage rebalances the pool, the relative value difference is 2×sqrt(r)/(1+r)−1 under these assumptions. At r=2 this is about −5.72%; at r=5 it is about −25.46%. This difference is a comparison with holding, not necessarily an absolute cash loss. Fees, incentives, concentrated ranges and token behavior change outcomes. Withdrawing does not create the earlier economic difference; a later price change can narrow or widen it. Smart-contract and custody risks are additional.

HOW IT WORKS

Impermanent loss compares the value of a liquidity-provider position with simply holding the original tokens. The difference depends on the pool design and relative prices; fees and incentives also matter.

KEY POINTS
Value difference between LP position and simply holding the tokens
In a simple fee-free constant-product pool, the relative value difference grows as paired-token prices diverge
The value difference exists before withdrawal and can change with subsequent prices
💡 WHY THIS MATTERS

Compare liquidity provision with holding the same initial assets under a stated pool model. Fees, incentives and price changes all matter, alongside contract and withdrawal risks.

Worked exercise and its limits

For a fee-free full-range constant-product pool initially holding 1 token worth $100 and $100 cash, double the token price. Arbitrage gives about 0.7071 tokens and $141.42 cash, total $282.84 versus $300 holding: about 5.72% less. Fees, incentives and concentrated liquidity change the comparison.

References and scope
Uniswap v2 — liquidity-provider returns and comparison with holding
